It's appropriate that we take a moment and recognize that all holiness is built on the reality of God.  God is holy love, at his core and essence.  In heaven, scenes from the Bible tell us that special creations like angels around the Throne of God call out "Holy, holy, holy," continually.  This Trinitarian repetition of HOLY is significant, because it's 3 in 1, and also because it's the only thing that's repeated around God's throne in this way.  He is faithful, he is powerful, he is knowledgeable, but in his essence -- he is Holy.  

What is that? He is separate, other, not like.  He is untouched by the faults and weakness and dependence of all other things.  He is completely other than His creation.  There are only 2 things in all existence: God & the Creation.  God & everything else.  That utter unique, separate purity is his holiness.  

Out of this, flow his other attributes. 
Everything else is unfaithful eventually, but God is faithfulness unmixed.  
Everything else is dependent & needy, God is completely un-needy, utterly independent.  
Everything else has a spot of corruption, but God is purity unmixed.
Everything else has it's light and darkness, its "yin and yang" -- but God is completely unmixed, completely single and whole,  utterly alone in his degree of perfection.

This holiness is often expressed as incomprehensible, utterly blinding, terrifying light in Scripture.  To be in the presence of God's complete holiness would literally kill your physical body, as if you had been suddenly transported to 100 miles away from the sun.  You couldn't physically or spiritually take the glory of his holiness.  

I don't mean to suggest that God's holiness is a negative thing, as though it was a source of pain and fear.  

On the contrary, the holiness of God is so glorious, so joyful, so explosively brilliant, that it's beauty and goodness is what is overwhelming. The Bible tells us to "worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness."  Humans have often recognized that there is a place where joy is so overwhelming that it gets close to something like terror.  Like the sheer terror as you're about to descend the world's tallest, fastest roller coaster, the joyous terror of his holiness would simply overwhelm you in every way, physically, mentally, emotionally, and spiritually.  

It's not that it's so bad it's scary, it's that it's so good it's marvelously scary.

I'm not an iPhone guy, but I have noticed while shopping for my wife's iphone charger (yes, we are a house divided)...�
I have noticed that there are fake products out there that WORK for apple, but are not made by Apple.
If you're a mechanic, there are aftermarket parts that may or may not fit, then there are OEM parts... original equipment manufacturer... they FIT.

It's the same way in Holiness.
The only real thing comes from connection to God.
He's the OEM the original equipment manufacturer... and nothing else will really fit.

There is no intrinsic holiness in any person or thing.  Most versions of human religion teach that there is "intrinsic" holiness in some place, person, or thing.  That this person is holy, because of some quality THEY possess. 
This is a holy object, holy rock, holy place, holy ceremony, etc.  So we get titles like "His Holiness the Dalai Lama" or "Holy Father" about the Pope. 

But when the Bible uses the word, that's not what it means.  The Bible teaches that there is no such thing as intrinsic holiness, that exists in a person or place or thing by themselves.

But when God comes into the picture, when he touches or uses something he communicates his holiness to and through that person or thing.  

Examples: 
Exodus 3 "The ground where you are standing is holy ground."  What made it holy?  Was it a special place?  No, just a bush and some wilderness ground.  But now, it's holy because God is using it. 
Bread is holy if God says it's for his use. 
Oil. 
Pots.
Sacrifices.
Day - The created or Mosaic Sabbath.
Gold. Matthew 23:17 Jesus asked the crowd: "Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes the gold sacred?"

In the Temple, God says the gold is holy, but Jesus says it's not holy on it's own -- The Temple makes it holy.  Why?  Because God has chosen to place his presence there.  He's there, so it's holy.

God's presence, touch, or use makes things holy that were not before.

So, so if Holiness is not a static quality, but a dynamic quality that only exists, only flows, as we have connection with God, what is the problem? What breaks the connection that brings holiness? if circuit, break the connection that brings holiness between us and God?

The answer is found in a foundational, classic passage on the holiness of God, Isaiah 6.  Isaiah sees the Lord, in his glory, the brilliant overwhelming beauty of his holiness.  
6 In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord, high and exalted, seated on a throne; and the train of his robe filled the temple. 2 Above him were seraphim, each with six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying. 3 And they were calling to one another:

“Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty;

    the whole earth is full of his glory.”

4 At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook and the temple was filled with smoke.

5 “Woe to me!” I cried. “I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Almighty.”

What Isaiah felt in that moment was the fact that he wasn't like what he saw.  He realized that what was separating him from God was not his ethnicity, or his background, or his lack of knowledge... it was his own heart, exemplified in this passage by his mouth... 

Isaiah had been speaking in chapters 1-5, saying "woe" to this one, or that one, wicked people or wicked nations.  But when he gets into the presence of God, he calls out "woe to me."  

There's an old story of a young child who was riding with his father through the country in the summer.  He saw sheep in the field, and said, "Oh, look at how white those sheep are in the green grass."  A few months later he drove through the same place after a blanket of snow had fallen.  He said, "Oh, look at those dirty sheep against that white snow."  The sheep hadn't changed... only what he compared them to.  

Isaiah is having a moment like this.  He hadn't changed... but now he was seeing himself in the light of God's holiness.

He felt the separation, the distance, the overwhelm of the reality that he was unworthy.  Now, it's important to remember here, that the reason for this is not that God's holiness is a negative, but that it's so good, so beautiful, so desirable, that nothing else can compare to the joy and delight of knowing it, of being connected to it.  It's as if you were a starving man at a feast, locked behind a gate, kept from that which is most desirable.

So the 2nd element of holiness is this: Holiness requires ongoing moral excellence in heart and action.

My wife and my dad both love puzzles.  A lot of times over family Christmas, there will be puzzle pieces spread over the dining room table.  You know what one of the first things they do? Put the puzzle box lid up where they can see it. It helps them see where the pieces go whe they can get the big picture. 

Who is primarily responsible for your holiness?  Whose idea was it?  

Ephesians 1:4 "...for he chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless in his sight."

Before the foundation of the world, God made a decision about what he would do with all those who trusted in his son.

God decided that we would be holy. Before any humans even existed, or before light was created, before there was a planet called Earth, God had already decided what he would do with those who trust in Jesus. If you are a believer in Jesus, God decreed that you would become holy, eternity past.

First, This means that your holiness was not your idea, it was not something you sought to put in place. It was not your idea, so you can relax about whether or not you are invited to the Holiness party that is the Christian family.

Secondly, it means that the initiative for creating a holiness in you is not yours. The initiative always lies with God. He started the whole Enterprise. 

Third, I want you to notice that we will be holy in his sight. This means that you will be holy in the sight of the One who is infinitely knowledgeable, infinitely wise, and infinitely powerful. You will be holy in the sight of the one who is the source of all holiness, and knows every part of you perfectly.  It does not mean you will always be holy in the sight of people around you, or that you will even be holy in your own sight.  Your holiness, remember is not a function of how you are thought of by others, your source of holiness is not yourself.

Fourth, I want you to notice that it was decided in eternity past.  All of recorded time has been in the light of God's Eternal decision, and so you need to know something about the short part of history that we call your life... 

All of your life, all of your struggles, all of your trouble, every single second of your existence up until now, has been leading up to you being holy. Every second of your existence from now until you breathe your last, is going to be exclusively about God bringing about his plan to make you holy.

Today, we're going to talk about the book of Leviticus.  

Pretty much nobody says, "Yeah! I can't wait to read the book of Leviticus! Good times!"  But Leviticus is a vital book to understanding what God means by holiness.  It's a primer on the subject, full of basic thoughts and definition that informs the rest of our education on the ideas of holiness.

People usually kind of "run down" Leviticus, and call it boring, or irrelevant, or basically read it and say, "Man! Thank God we don't have to do all that stuff any more!" But if you've read Leviticus, there's a good chance that you've been puzzled by the many seemingly strange or silly laws in the Old Testament.

"So you can distinguish between the holy and the common, between the clean and the unclean." (Lev. 10:10)

Is very important to remember that God did not accept one type of animal, or one type of clothing, and call it holy, because of anything in itself.  Sheep were not holy because they were ... more holier than other animals. � 

Remember, God is the source of all Holiness, so he was not saying that they needed to understand the difference between intrinsically holy things, and those that were not. He was teaching that all things are common except what he has made holy. And whatever God has made holy, is no longer common.

Have you ever seen the yin-yang symbol?  It's a universal symbol in eastern religions.  It's basic idea is that there is dark and light balance in the universe, and in all light there is some dark and in all dark there is some light.  Eastern spiritual teachers came to this conclusion through their study of the universe, and it's kind of a natural conclusion to come to.  

Everything else in the universe has yin and yang, some good, some not. Some strength, some weakness.  Some dark, some light.

Everything else is mixed.  And that mixture includes moral corruption.  This can be in our actions, like stealing, lying, or murder.  

But yin/yang doesn't explain the Universe.  

Here's why: God isn't mixed.  He is utterly, unimaginably pure, completely incorruptible.

When God calls us to be holy like He is, he is telling us that he requires us to be untouched by that which brings corruption.  
So God taught this kind of holiness in Leviticus, by making it a violation of his holiness to be touched by a dead body, or infection, or unclean animal.  

If we want to know God, we must to be free from evil actions, from the guilt of sin.  
" But your iniquities have separated you from your God; your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he will not hear." Isaiah 59:2

But the corruption of sin goes deeper than just actions.  It goes down into motivations.

This is why Jesus teachings were so revolutionary.  He taught in such a way that he exposed the heart of people.  When he taught, he showed it was possible to do even right things for wrong motives.  

There's lie mixed with honesty, greed mixed with ambition, self mixed with selflessness.  Jesus even taught there can be pride mixed with giving, and arrogance mixed with prayer.  In other words, even "good" actions can be mixed with morally corrupting influence.

I have a math problem for you to solve. OK? GO! 

You can't solve a problem if you don't know what the problem is.

When your car breaks down, ever stood staring into the engine compartment.... hoping something will fix itself?  Dave Barry says, "I stare  thoughtfully into the engine compartment.  I don't know what I"m looking for. I always hope it will be something obvious like a squid clinging to the manifold."

Some of you are trying to solve the problem called YOU. Trying to solve you has lost you 10 or 20 years, 2-3 relationships, jobs... 

Do you really need someone to tell you "don't look at that stuff, it just pollutes your mind and wrecks your relationships"

Do you really need someone to tell you "that substance is going to steal your happiness, wreck your body and make everything worse?"

Do you really need someone to tell you "pay now, play later?" 

No, the problem isn't that WE DON'T KNOW WHAT TO DO... it's that we can't do.

Maybe the problem is that you don't know what the problem is.

So stick with me for the next couple days, because we're going to take a hard look into the engine compartment and see what the problem is.

Tim McGraw, Cowboy in me: 
I don't know why I act the way I do,
Like I ain't got a single thing to lose.  
Sometimes, I'm my own worst enemy. 
I guess that's just the cowboy in me...

The urge to run, the restlessness,
The heart of stone, I sometimes get.
The things I've done for foolish pride,
The "me" that's never satisfied. 
The face that's in the mirror when I don't like what I see. (Cowboy in Me, written by Al Anderson, Craig Wiseman, and Jeffrey Steele)

That's a pretty good explanation of the sin nature.

People who are not Christians try to explain away their sinful nature by blaming it on their spouse, their personality, their upbringing, their parents didn't potty train them right when they were 3. �  

And sometimes, people who are Christians try to explain it away by the same methods.  They just rename it.  
I'm not angry and yelling, I'm speaking forcefully because I'm righteously indignant. 
I'm not gossiping, I'm sharing prayer needs.
I'm not speaking unkindly, I'm just bringing the truth no one else dares to say. 
I'm not proud, I've just got really great self-image.
I'm not worrying, I'm just... 
You get the idea.

Now here's the thing: 
This sinful nature is hardwired into your mind, your soul, your psyche.  It's not like a bolt-on, or a plug in, it's part of the operating system.  

In theology, it's called the "sin nature."  It's a noun that results in verbs.  It's a sin that results in sinning.  All sin flows from it. 

Let's look at it in Scripture: 
Psalm 58:3 Even from birth the wicked go astray; from the womb, they are wayward, spreading lies."

I imagine you remember playing hide-and seek when you were a kid.  Do you remember the best place you ever found to hide?  That one place that no one could see, no one could find?  

The sinful nature is good at hide and seek.  Today, my goal is to help you pull back the camouflage and see behind it, to catch what's really going on. 
Jeremiah 17:9 says "The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure.  Who can understand it?"  Now, I'll come back to that statement of "beyond cure" later, but I want you to not miss the last phrase -- "who can understand it?"  The implication is that we can't understand it.  The sinful nature is a master of disguise, and 

--it remains in the heart after salvation. 

Salvation is powerful, wonderful and great.  It's amazing to be saved, forgiven of sin, and be a new creation.  What that means it that you completely start over, your guilt is gone, your conscience is cleansed, you are raised from death to life and adopted into God's family.  

But every theological system from every denomination recognizes that this is the case: The "cowboy in me", the Nature of Sin, remains.   
Catholics, Presbyterians, Pentecostals, Methodists, Baptists, and more. They ALL believe that.  It's hard to get 5 different denominations in a room and have them agree on things, right?  But they all recognize this one as true.

We have actions of sin, but behind them is the nature of sin itself, and that nature remains after the actions are forgiven.  It is bound, it is weakened, it is not ruling, but it is present.

So what is this sin nature?

It's a warping of the human spirit by the absence of the sanctifying presence of the Creator.  Adam and Eve didn't have something added to them as much as they LOST something.  They were holy by the continual connection they had to God.  In Adam, we are conceived and born sinful.  
It's a noun that results in verbs.  It's THE Sin that results in SINS.

Maybe you're wondering if this is something that I'm just making up, or if other people have noticed this.  Let me read you some lyrics from a song: 
John Mayer, Gravity: 
Gravity is working against me
And gravity wants to bring me down
Oh, I'll never known what makes this man
With all the love that his heart can stand
Dream of ways to throw it all away
Whoa, gravity is working against me
And gravity wants to bring me down
Oh, twice as much ain't twice as good
And can't sustain like one half could
It's wanting more -- gonna send me to my knees

Wow. This guy knows.  He's struggled with it -- he calls it "gravity" that's pulling him down, but it's the sin nature.
Isaiah said, "We have turned every one into HIS OWN WAY."

I want to start with a secular song by John Mayer, called "In the Blood"  Listen as he wrestles with his heart and how it keeps him tied to bad in his life:  

How much of my mother has my mother left in me?
How much of my love will be insane to some degree?
And what about this feeling that I'm never good enough?
Will it wash out in the water, or is it always in the blood?
How much of my father am I destined to become?
Will I dim the lights inside me just to satisfy someone?
Will I let this woman kill me, or do away with jealous love?
Will it wash out in the water, or is it always in the blood?
I can feel love the I want, I can feel the love I need
But it's never gonna come the way I am
Could I change it if I wanted, can I rise above the flood?
Will it wash out in the water, or is it always in the blood?

Do you feel what John Mayer is struggling with here?  Is it just IN ME?  Is it IN MY BLOOD?  Can I ever get rid of these things? 

John, I know what you need.  You need better blood.  You need some blood flowing in your veins that was shed 2,000 years ago. 
"And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood." Hebrews 13:12 (NIV older)  

God is holy. 
God requires holiness, he wills it for his people.
God taught us about holiness.
But our own nature of unholiness means we can't create it, or reach it.

But God decided to provide it.

He provided judicial holiness through justification, by imputing to us the righteousness of Christ, his obedience for our sin.  This is when he declares us not guilty. Zechariah 14:20 On that day holy to the Lord will be inscribed on the bells of the horses, and the cooking pots in the Lord’s house will be like the sacred bowls in front of the altar. 21 Every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the Lord Almighty, and all who come to sacrifice will take some of the pots and cook in them. And on that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty.

Holiness is so integral to the plan of God that he intends to make all things holy.  

In the Old Testament, God begins moving closer and helping His People understand what he means when he says "I am holy."  Because the Blood of Christ was not yet shed to provide holiness, God creates barriers, walls that contain his holiness -- a Tabernacle, a temple.  He creates things that are specially cleansed, specially washed, specially consecrated by the blood of bulls and goats.  He sets apart a certain race, a certain priesthood to interface his holiness.  

But through his servants the prophets, looking down through time, He points out a day that things will be different.  

Someday, the line between what is holy and what is common will be erased... not so that everything will be common, but so that everything will be holy.  

We are privileged to erase this line today -- to see God's future plans for His Kingdom, come to pass in our hearts and our lives NOW.  By the power of God's Holy Spirit, we live out NOW God's eternal purpose for the destination of the universe: That everything NOW can be holy.  That everything NOW that is common can be sanctified to God's ownership.  That everything NOW that is corrupted can be put away, and everything in my heart be holy to the Lord.

Psalm 86:11  Teach me your way, Lord,
    that I may rely on your faithfulness;
give me an undivided heart,
    that I may fear your name.

The same word (Hebrew: echad) translated “undivided” is used in 
1 Chronicles 12:38 All these were fighting men who volunteered to serve in the ranks. 
They came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. All the rest of the Israelites were also of one mind (Hebrew: echad) to make David king.
1.	David saw something in himself, by the insight the Holy Spirit gave him.
He realized that his heart was divided. This picture of the heart is consistent with the rest of Scripture. 

When we are unsaved, we are people of one nature, nothing but evil. But when we are saved, we are raised to new life by Christ, and we become people of competing natures -- a regenerated nature of spiritual life, and a nature of sin that will unfailingly lead us toward sin & death. 

When our heart is divided, it prevents us from consistently living in the fear of the Lord.
 “…by the fear of the LORD men depart from evil.” (Proverbs 16:6, KJV)
2.	David was drawn by the Holy Spirit to pray that this division would be healed by God's power. 
I want to point out that this wasn't just David being overly dramatic, or asking for something that wasn't the Lord's will. The Holy Spirit inspired David to ask this!

Now, I know there are two kinds of people watching this: 
People who have maybe heard of "holiness churches" and you're not sure what that is, or if it's some kind of cult or something.  You're wondering if this really Gospel, or if it's some fringe teaching... is it Pentecostal?  Do I have to handle snakes? Do I have to become a Methodist?  Or maybe you're wondering if you have to leave your church or something in order to learn about holiness and see it grow in your life.  Relax.  I'm interested in you being holy no matter where you are, and growing in that holiness for the rest of your life.  This isn't about a denomination, it's about a quality of life with God.  That's what I want for you. Everything else is details.

Another group of people are here who are FROM holiness churches, and you're a bit confused... you've heard different things about the doctrine of holiness. Sometimes it's been confusing & frustrating. Some people have been around you who lived it, but didn't teach how very well.  Other people around you may have taught it, but when it came to their life, they really didn't live it. Sometimes people preached it in ways that really didn't connect with you, and you're kind of wandering theologically, trying to figure out where you’re going to land. This 40 day journey is going to be helpful to you, as well. 

Both of those groups, here's what I'd like you to do:  Put aside your pre-suppositions for a minute and let me say this... all I want is for you to be as much like Jesus as possible.  That's it.  That's what holiness means.  So if you're up for that journey, stick with me.  We'll build a biblical theology of what it means to be holy, and how Jesus grows our holiness, and we'll chase it together for these 40 days.  I think what you'll discover is, that this isn't as complicated as you thought, it's a way full of joy and passion for God and his Gospel and his character in our lives.

If you've been raised in a holiness church and you're wondering whether or not to give it another shot, stick with me. For the next 40 days, set aside your assumptions and what you thought you know, and what you've been taught and confused about... and just flow with this.  

Here's a word about theology and terms:
Theology is amazing. It’s the study of the greatest, most ultimate Being, the most all-satisfying Reality in the universe. But sometimes, theology can be frustrating or confusing, especially if it doesn’t seem to match up to the Scripture. This is my attempt to teach what is possible for God to do in your heart by using Scripture and its words, with as few theological and category words as I can. As much as possible, I'm going to just let the scripture shape both the container and the holiness content that we're going to put in it.

This is a 40 day journey... watch your daily video, pray over it, meditate on the question of the day, and let's pursue holiness together.

I'm excited to get started!

Blessings,

Darrell L. Stetler II
Oklahoma City, OK
